_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head-term for the generic fancy-text generator job; already the H1/title of the flagship NL page. Use as the default umbrella term when no more specific style is meant.
phrases.good_example: Gratis lettertype generator: mooie letters, sierletters, aesthetic fonts en coole symbolen om te kopiëren en plakken.
phrases.avoid_when: when the specific style being discussed is bold, script, or gothic — use the more specific term instead

phrases.usage_guidance: Correct, natural Dutch term for calligraphic/script-style Unicode letters. On the homepage FAQ this is explicitly distinguished from 'schuine letters (cursief/italic)' — keep that separation intact when writing copy that discusses both. || REVISED 2026-07-26: lead with the CLOSED COMPOUND 'sierletters', not the adjectival 'sierlijke letters' -- GSC shows the compound outperforming the adjectival ~3:1 on impressions (441 vs 145). Keep both in the title; the compound goes first. The sierletters/schuine-letters disambiguation above still stands.
phrases.good_example: Sierletters voor namen en quotes (𝓁𝒾𝑒𝓋𝑒 𝓋𝒾𝒷𝑒𝓈)
phrases.avoid_when: when italic/slanted text (not script/calligraphic) is meant — use 'schuine letters' instead

phrases.usage_guidance: In standard Dutch, 'cursief' is the everyday and typographically correct word for italic (slanted) text — it is NOT the natural Dutch word for flowing calligraphic/script handwriting style. The site's own homepage FAQ and Discord formatting guide both use it this way correctly ('Wat is het verschil met gewoon vet of cursief typen?'; Discord markdown '*cursief*' -> real italic). Use 'cursief' when the real italic slant (native formatting or the italic-fonts Unicode set) is meant.
phrases.good_example: *cursief* -> cursief (Discord markdown italic)
phrases.avoid_when: do not use 'cursief' as the label for the script/handwriting-style Unicode font family — see NL-004 for the site's own internal conflict on this point

phrases.usage_guidance: Used interchangeably with 'cursief' on the homepage ('schuine letters (cursief / italic)') and independently ('schuine sierletters', 'schuine fonts'). Natural, safe synonym for italic; also combines with sierletters to describe the aesthetic-tilted script look used in TikTok captions.
phrases.good_example: Voor captions worden vooral schuine sierletters en kleine hoofdletters (sᴍᴀʟʟ ᴄᴀᴘs) gebruikt

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary, natural umbrella term for symbols/glyphs; matches the dedicated library hub. See NL-020 'vreemde tekens' for a natural near-synonym used more in a troubleshooting/rendering-failure context.
phrases.good_example: Waarom zie ik soms een vierkantje (□) in plaats van een teken?

phrases.english_concept: boxes/squares shown instead of a glyph (tofu rendering failure)
phrases.usage_guidance: This is one of the most heavily reused FAQ answers on the whole NL site — near-identical 'vierkantje (□) betekent dat het toestel... niet kent' phrasing appears on at least 8 different pages. It is the correct, natural Dutch term for this failure mode and should keep being reused verbatim/near-verbatim for consistency. 'Blokjes' is used as a casual synonym in the same sentence on nl/mooie-letters/.
phrases.good_example: Een vierkantje (□) betekent dat het toestel van de lezer dat specifieke teken niet kent — vaak een ouder toestel of een verouderde app.

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary, natural, already-live term for this feature; the dedicated page also naturally uses 'lege spatie', 'blokje' (for a failed/rejected invisible char) and 'schijnbaar leeg WhatsApp-bericht'.
phrases.good_example: Kopieer een onzichtbaar teken en plak het in de Instagram-bio voor lege regels of nette witruimte, of stuur het als een schijnbaar leeg WhatsApp-bericht.

phrases.usage_guidance: This distinction matters functionally: Unicode styling works in the weergavenaam but is stripped from the strict a-z/0-9 @gebruikersnaam handle. The Discord guide gets this exactly right and should be the model for any other platform page that needs to explain the same username-vs-display-name split.
phrases.good_example: De @gebruikersnaam weigert het. [...] Style in plaats daarvan je weergavenaam.

phrases.usage_guidance: Standard Dutch word for a server-level nickname (as opposed to weergavenaam/gebruikersnaam, see NL-009). Also the standard word used site-wide in Dutch tech press for changing a Discord nickname.
phrases.good_example: Mijn weergavenaam of bijnaam stylen

phrases.usage_guidance: Primary, natural, already-live term for the bold category page.
phrases.good_example: n/a — page title term

phrases.usage_guidance: Standard, correct, everyday Dutch verb pair — used consistently site-wide and by every Dutch competitor tool. No natural slang alternative needed; do not substitute 'knippen en plakken' (cut and paste), which is a different action.
phrases.good_example: Druk op kopiëren, plak het in je bio, caption of WhatsApp, klaar.
phrases.avoid_when: do not confuse with 'knippen en plakken' (cut and paste)

phrases.usage_guidance: Natural, standard term, already live on the bio-font usecase page ('Live preview en tekenlimieten voor Instagram, TikTok, Discord...'). Confirmed as the term Dutch character-counter tools also use as their own brand name (tekenstellen.nl).
phrases.good_example: Live preview en tekenlimieten voor Instagram, TikTok, Discord, X, WhatsApp, Facebook & Tinder

phrases.usage_guidance: Natural, direct translation, used correctly alongside 'stoer/edgy' register on the homepage's gaming-names FAQ answer.
phrases.good_example: Gotische letters (𝔡𝔞𝔯𝔨𝔚𝔬𝔩𝔣), zalgo voor horror-vibes, doorgestreepte tekst voor een 'glitched' look.

phrases.usage_guidance: Natural direct translation, already live as a dedicated page title; the borrowed English term 'small caps' is kept parenthetically alongside it site-wide, which matches how the term is actually used by Dutch audiences (both forms circulate).
phrases.good_example: kleine hoofdletters (sᴍᴀʟʟ ᴄᴀᴘs)

phrases.usage_guidance: Kept untranslated on purpose — the homepage FAQ explicitly explains it rather than translating it ('Met "aesthetic letters" bedoelen de meeste mensen die rustige, fijne look...'), which matches how the word is actually used by young Dutch social-media users: as an unglossed English loanword, not calqued into Dutch. Do not force a Dutch translation like 'esthetisch' in this context register — that reads stiff/formal, not native usage.
phrases.good_example: Wat zijn aesthetic letters en hoe krijg ik die look?

phrases.usage_guidance: Borrowed English term, unchanged and unhyphenated-or-hyphenated interchangeably; already live and natural. Corroborated by both Dutch (gtagames.nl forum: 'namen met tekens erin') and international clan-tag symbol resources.
phrases.good_example: Symbolen met één teken voor een clan-tag, zwaard-naam of gedurfde display name.

phrases.native_phrase: vraagteken in een vierkantje / vraagteken in een blokje
phrases.english_concept: question mark in a box (rendering failure, specifically the NBSP/tofu variant)
phrases.usage_guidance: A specific, real variant of the general 'vierkantje' rendering-failure phrasing (NL-007) worth using verbatim in troubleshooting FAQ copy for users who search the symptom rather than the cause. Site already covers the general case; this is the more specific symptom-first search formulation.
phrases.good_example: Kan iemand mij vertellen waar dat vraagteken voorstaat? In Excel komt deze niet voor.

phrases.english_concept: strange/odd characters (near-synonym of special characters, skews troubleshooting)
phrases.usage_guidance: Natural near-synonym of 'speciale tekens' (NL-006) but with a troubleshooting/confusion connotation rather than a browse/discovery one — fits an answer-style FAQ ('why do I see vreemde tekens') better than a library hub title. A dedicated Dutch competitor site (vreemdetekens.nl) uses this exact phrase as its brand name, confirming real independent search demand distinct from 'speciale tekens'.
phrases.good_example: Commando om vreemde tekens en symbolen uit woord te halen
phrases.avoid_when: do not use as the primary hub label (that's 'speciale tekens') — this fits FAQ/troubleshooting copy specifically

phrases.english_concept: symbols/characters used inside a name (generic, informal)
phrases.usage_guidance: Informal, generic way forum posters actually describe decorated gamertags without naming a specific symbol type ('¶' or '¥' were the examples given) — useful as a colloquial variant of 'symbolen/tekentjes voor in je naam' already in the prior batch's dictionary, confirming that pattern independently.
phrases.good_example: Soms zie ook namen met tekens erin zoals ¶ of ¥ (En meer natuurlijk)
phrases.avoid_when: too informal/vague for a page title — use 'symbolen/tekentjes voor in je naam' or 'speciale tekens' there instead

phrases.usage_guidance: Head a Dutch page with 'Japanse emoticons' (optionally + 'kaomoji' as the second term for the small share who know it). Reuse the quarter-turn framing verbatim in the explainer — it is how Dutch already talks about this and no MT competitor will produce it.
phrases.good_example: Bij Japanse emoticons hoef je je hoofd geen kwartslag te draaien — ze staan rechtop, in tegenstelling tot :-).
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use 'emoticons' where graphical emoji are meant. Don't build the page around 'kaomoji' as the sole head term — the Dutch recognition rate for it is low.

phrases.usage_guidance: Keep the hyphen — 'ASCII-art' is the correct Dutch orthography and the unhyphenated 'ASCII art' is a visible English-copy tell. Describe it in Dutch as 'afbeeldingen uit tekens'.
phrases.good_example: ASCII-art: afbeeldingen die volledig uit tekens zijn samengesteld, klaar om te kopiëren naar Discord of een chat.
phrases.avoid_when: Not for single face emoticons. Avoid in copy aimed at very young/school audiences where the term won't be known.

phrases.usage_guidance: Lead with 'kopregel' in Dutch body copy; keeping 'headline' in the title is legitimate here rather than lazy, because Dutch users genuinely search the English word.
phrases.good_example: Op mobiel stopt je kopregel na zo'n 40-50 tekens.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'koptekst' — that is a document header (Word), not a LinkedIn field. Do not use it for a bio on other platforms.

phrases.english_concept: professional-risk objection: over-styled text looks shouty and unprofessional
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in a moderation/honesty section that acknowledges the objection before giving restrained guidance ('een of twee woorden'). Pairs naturally with 'met mate' (sparingly).
phrases.good_example: Te veel symbolen, emoji of hoofdletters komen al snel schreeuwerig en onprofessioneel over.
phrases.avoid_when: Wrong register for gaming or aesthetic pages — NL-017 (stoer) territory has its own vocabulary. Do not use it to describe a single styled word; it describes excess.

phrases.english_concept: screen reader (assistive technology) — the accessibility objection
phrases.content_surface: faq, body copy, accessibility disclosure section
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'schermlezer' as the noun and name the people ('mensen met een visuele beperking') in the same sentence — Dutch accessibility writing does this consistently and it reads as informed rather than box-ticking. Concrete is better than abstract: quote what the reader actually hears.
phrases.good_example: In plaats van het woord te lezen, leest de schermlezer elk teken als zijn Unicode-naam voor: 'wiskundig vet h, wiskundig vet e...'
phrases.avoid_when: Never in gaming/aesthetic copy as a throwaway. Do not use an accessibility claim as a selling point for the tool — it is a limitation to disclose, not a feature.

phrases.english_concept: the line-break / blank-line action that produces stacked text in a bio or caption
phrases.register: witregel: neutral, safe anywhere. entertjes: casual/affectionate, body copy only
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq heading, tool copy, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use «witregels» in the heading and tool label, «entertjes» at most once in body copy where the tone is friendly. Distinguish the two things Dutch sources distinguish: «van lijn veranderen» (just go to the next line) versus a «witregel» (a full blank line), and note that a blank line costs characters — Dutch sources raise that trade-off explicitly and Dutch readers respond to it.
phrases.good_example: Zo krijg je witregels in je Instagram bio — zonder dat je hele tekst weer aan elkaar plakt.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use «entertjes» in formal, legal, accessibility or technical copy. Do not use «verticale tekst» for this concept — it imports a typographic sense the Dutch market does not mean here.

phrases.native_phrase: je hele tekst plakt weer aan elkaar vast
phrases.english_concept: the platform merging the stacked lines back into one block
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the Dutch FAQ heading or the opening line of the answer, so the page repeats the user's own sentence back to them, then give the fix (draft elsewhere and paste, or use an invisible character — NL-008).
phrases.good_example: Je zet er netjes entertjes tussen, je plaatst je bericht en hop: je hele tekst plakt weer aan elkaar vast.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a title/H1 term. Do not use it for glyph-level failures (boxes, unsupported characters) — different problem, different fix. Avoid in formal/technical copy where the playful 'hop' register would jar.

phrases.native_phrase: instagram bio symbolen / instagram bio tekens
phrases.english_concept: Instagram bio symbol/character decoration (the search-formulation pattern, not a single term)
phrases.usage_guidance: Dutch searchers and competitors consistently append "bio" to "symbolen/tekens" rather than searching a bare "instagram symbolen" (which returns mostly English-tool results). If a Dutch translation of library/instagram-symbols is ever built, lead the title/H1 with the bio-qualified compound, not a literal rendering of the EN slug.
phrases.good_example: Instagram Bio Symbolen ✦ — kopiëren en plakken.
phrases.avoid_when: do not use a bare "instagram symbolen" as the primary H1/title — it under-targets what Dutch users actually type

phrases.usage_guidance: Dutch uses the diminutive vinkje (not vink) — vinkje symbool 1,600/mo; both nl/library/vinkje and nl/symbol/vinkje-symbool are already slugged on it.
phrases.avoid_when: Not for the verb sense (aanvinken = to tick a box) in UI-instruction copy.
